Liji 30 · Zi Yi 緇衣 · The Black Robes · Zi Yi 13 … Zi Yi 19

items.text: Do not for the sake of a favorite concubine provoke your queen.
items.quote: do not for the sake of a favourite concubine provoke queen Kwang
items.conflict: Polygamy is contrary to Scripture (Genesis 2:24; Matthew 19:4-6).

items.text: Be correct in personal character when serving your superior, so that your words may be believed.
items.quote: if his personal character be not correct, his words will not be believed

heading: Liji 30 · Zi Yi 緇衣 · The Black Robes · Zi Yi 1 … Zi Yi 12

items.text: Love those below you as your own children.
Bind them to yourself by good faith, so they will not turn away.
items.quote: when he binds them to himself by his good faith, they do not turn away from him

items.text: Preside over them with courtesy, so their hearts are docile.
items.quote: when he presides over them with courtesy, their hearts are docile to him

items.text: Be careful in what you like and dislike, for you are their example.
items.quote: Therefore the superior should by all means be careful in what he likes and dislikes. This will make him an example to the people.

items.text: Lead them on to good by your words, and keep them from evil by your conduct.
items.quote: The superior man leads men on (to good) by his words, and keeps them (from evil) by (the example of) his conduct.

items.text: Let your words and deeds agree, so that your words can be carried into action and your actions spoken of.
items.quote: The superior does not speak words which may be spoken indeed but should not be embodied in deeds; nor does he do actions which may be done in deed but should not be expressed in words.

items.text: Exhibit clearly what you love and guard against what you dislike, to keep them from going astray.
items.quote: when the ruler exhibits clearly what he loves, and thus shows the people the style of manners (they should aim at), and is watchful against what he dislikes, and thereby guards the people against the excesses

items.text: Give distinction to the righteous and make it painful for the bad, showing them the excellence to cultivate.
items.quote: When the holders of states and clans give distinction to the righteous and make it painful for the bad, thus showing the people the excellence (they should cultivate)

items.text: Use no improper variations in dress and keep your manners easy, to give uniformity to the people.
items.quote: When the heads of the people use no (improper) variations in their dress, and their manners are always easy and unconstrained, and they seek thus to give uniformity to the people

items.text: Be exemplary in conduct, avoid fine speeches, and do not trouble your superior with unattainable or unknowable demands.
items.quote: When the ministers are exemplary in their conduct, and do not set a value on (fine) speeches; when they do not try to lead (the ruler) to what is unattainable, and do not trouble him with what cannot be (fully) known
